title: P48: 0.01 pretraining entropy bonus on the five-layer incumbent
description: P48 follow-up: add a predictive-entropy reward of 0.01 to the unchanged supervised-token pretraining loss of incumbent 051-claude, retaining its five-layer architecture. This tests whether the modest four-layer entropy benefit composes with increased depth to improve fixed downstream expert iteration.
hypothesis: The five-layer incumbent 051-claude scores 288/260/311 (exact mean 286.333333). On the earlier four-layer 043-codex baseline, P48 coefficient 0.01 in 052-codex raised the mean by 5 solves (292/300/249 versus 282/275/269), while 0.02 in 053-codex hurt all three seeds (202/262/210). This is weak, mixed-seed evidence for the smaller coefficient, not evidence of a monotonic benefit. No prior registration tests 0.01 with five layers. Adding only this smaller distribution-dependent entropy reward may preserve plausible alternative continuations while the extra layer supplies the rule-checking capacity, improving first-round discovery and the final fixed-RL dev-transfer mean. The interaction could instead be adverse: a deeper model has fewer pretraining updates at fixed wall-clock and may lose syntax precision. Every existing supervised token is treated uniformly; data, token selection, sampling temperature, and downstream RL loss remain unchanged. Only the frozen three-seed downstream mean decides keep/discard.
expected_delta: Central prediction +3 to +15 dev-transfer solves at true length >=7 relative to 051-claude exact mean 286.333333, with round-1 RL sample accuracy improving on at least two seeds from 0.0630/0.0494/0.0749; plausible downside -40. Expect 0-3% fewer pretraining updates than 2320/2370/2341 because of the entropy calculation, unchanged 4,000,000 parameters and identical inference operations. Total duration should remain approximately 940-1080 seconds per seed under the 1200-second cap; changed sampled lengths can affect runtime. Ordinary CE validation is diagnostic, while training loss includes the entropy reward.

arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon hidden matrices throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) are in Muon. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 remain unchanged.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, head.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters throughout; hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction, including the former finish window; integrated decay can differ with throughput.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter after moving to device. Gain = 0.02 * sqrt(max(rows, columns)); exact element second moment 0.0004. All 20 hidden matrices: qkv (768,256), proj (256,256), fc1 (1024,256), fc2 (256,1024) in each of five blocks. QKV initialized jointly. Embedding and readout keep the fork's normal(0.02) draws; biases zero; LayerNorm weight 1 and bias 0. No reinitialization during RL. The fifth block consumes extra global-RNG draws during construction, so random initial weights are not bitwise identical to 043's for a given seed; the init rule is identical.

loss.name: supervised next-token cross-entropy minus predictive entropy
loss.mask: unchanged shifted proof mask, including every supervised termination token
loss.reduction: sum of masked per-token CE minus 0.01 times categorical entropy, divided by supervised token count
loss.precision: logits converted to float32 before cross-entropy and log_softmax
loss.handoff: loss function used only by pretrain(); fork GPT forward and frozen RL loss unchanged
